flags: Hasbro recognized a non-cash goodwill impairment of $1,021.9 million in the Consumer Products segment in the second quarter of 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Hasbro generates revenue by developing, marketing, licensing, and selling physical and digital games, video games, toys, licensed consumer products, location-based entertainment, film, and television based on owned and partner intellectual property.
quotes: With over 100 years of expertise, we deliver play experiences to kids, families, and fans around the world, through physical and digital games, video games, toys, licensed consumer products, location-based entertainment, film, TV and more.

We generate revenue and earn cash by developing, marketing, licensing and selling products, play and entertainment experiences, based on our global brands as well as other IP in a broad variety of categories.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business.
business_model.claim: Its brand portfolio combines owned and controlled franchises such as MAGIC: THE GATHERING, MONOPOLY, PLAY-DOH, TRANSFORMERS, DUNGEONS & DRAGONS, NERF, and PEPPA PIG with third-party licensed brands including MARVEL, STAR WARS, BEYBLADE, and Final Fantasy.
quotes: Through our franchise-first approach, we unlock value from both new and legacy IP, including MAGIC: THE GATHERING, MONOPOLY, HASBRO GAMES, PLAY-DOH, TRANSFORMERS, DUNGEONS & DRAGONS, NERF, and PEPPA PIG, as well as premier partner brands.
Additionally, through license agreements with third parties, we develop and sell products based on popular third-party brands through these channels.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 7 MD&A.
business_model.claim: Hasbro out-licenses its brands and intellectual property to third parties for consumer products, digital games such as MONOPOLY GO!, and capital-efficient location-based entertainment such as theme parks.
quotes: Hasbro is one of the world’s largest and most diverse licensors, and a growing part of our Playing to Win strategy is to extend the reach of our brands through the out-licensing of our intellectual properties to third parties for consumer products, digital games and entertainment.

These experiences bring our brands to life and further immerse our consumers in our storytelling in a capital efficient manner as the third-parties operating these experiences are making the investment in these initiatives.

business_model.basis: Stated in the third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A and Form 8-K earnings release tables.
business_model.claim: Revenue comes primarily from product net sales—$1,451.0 (table in millions, 91.0% of net revenues) in the third quarter of 2026 and $3,317.9 (table in millions, 88.8%) in the first nine months of 2026—supplemented by licensing revenue of 144.3 (table in millions, 9.0%) and 417.2 (table in millions, 11.2%), respectively.
quotes: Licensing revenue consists of royalties earned from the out-licensing of our trademarks, characters and other brand and intellectual property rights.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and Item 1A Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: Hasbro sells to kids, families, and fans worldwide through retail stores, ecommerce platforms, specialty hobby stores, and direct-to-consumer platforms including Hasbro PULSE, SECRET LAIR, Magic: The Gathering Arena, and D&D Beyond.
quotes: We market and sell toys and games based on our owned and controlled brands globally at retail stores, through ecommerce platforms and through our fan-based direct-to-consumer platforms Hasbro PULSE and SECRET LAIR.
Similarly, sales of certain products of our Wizards business depend in part on the success of specialty hobby stores.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors.
business_model.claim: Sales depend on a concentrated retail customer base—with Amazon.com, Inc. and Wal-Mart, Inc. accounting for approximately 11% and 9%, respectively, of 2025 consolidated net revenues—and customers generally order via purchase orders without binding long-term purchase commitments.
quotes: During 2025, Amazon.com, Inc. and Wal-Mart, Inc. accounted for approximately 11% and 9%, respectively, of our consolidated net revenues.
Our customers generally do not enter into binding long-term purchase commitments with us and make all purchases by delivering purchase orders.

quotes: The summary that follows provides a discussion of the results of operations of our segments: Wizards of the Coast & Digital Gaming, Consumer Products and Entertainment.
Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment operating profit increased $374.8 million to $1,006.8 million in 2025, compared to $632.0 million in 2024.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Items 1 and 7 and the third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Management organizes its brands under the Playing to Win strategy into Grow Brands, Optimize Brands, and Reinvent Brands, with Grow Brands accounting for $3,479.1 (table in millions) of $4,701.3 (table in millions) total net revenues in 2025 and $1,191.1 (table in millions) of $1,595.3 (table in millions) in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: As part of our Playing to Win strategy, we have realigned our brand portfolios to correspond our refreshed strategy:

Our Grow Brands represent the highest margin, highest growth opportunities in categories where we see significant share and/or underlying market growth, such as MAGIC: THE GATHERING, Hasbro Gaming, PLAY-DOH, Marvel, including SPIDER-MAN and THE AVENGERS, and DUNGEONS & DRAGONS.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A, third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A, and Form 8-K earnings release.
business_model.claim: Revenue growth is primarily driven by MAGIC: THE GATHERING—especially third-party Universes Beyond collaborations—which increased $641.5 million in 2025 and grew 34.1% (or $156.7 million) in the third quarter of 2026 to $616.1 (table in millions).
quotes: The net revenue increase primarily reflects higher net revenues from Magic: The Gathering, which grew by $156.7 million, or 34.1%, driven by strong performance of the Universes Beyond The Hobbit set released during the quarter, as well as Reality Fracture.
Magic: The Gathering Surpasses $600 million in Quarterly Revenue for First Time

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A, third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A, and Form 8-K earnings release.
business_model.claim: Digital licensing (led by MONOPOLY GO!, which contributed $168.0 million in 2025 and $127 million year-to-date in 2026) and entertainment-linked toy releases such as Marvel (up $46.8 million in the third quarter of 2026) and KPop Demon Hunters (up $13.3 million) also move revenue, alongside offsetting declines in legacy lines such as NERF and PEPPA PIG.
quotes: Growth in MAGIC: THE GATHERING was accompanied by an increase in MONOPOLY, both in the traditional games space, as well as from increased contributions from our digital licensing arrangement with Scopely, Inc. for MONOPOLY GO!, which contributed $168.0 million of revenue in 2025 compared to $112.2 million of revenue in 2024.

This growth within the Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment was supplemented by an increase in net sales within the Consumer Products segment, driven by an increase in toy and game sales for Marvel of $46.8 million as a result of a strong content slate, along with the introduction of new toys and games for the recently acquired KPop Demon Hunters license, which drove an increase of $13.3 million.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A Risk Factors and third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Revenue is also affected by shifting consumer tastes, seasonality, and operational disruptions such as the late March 2026 unauthorized network access that delayed order processing, shipping, and invoicing during the second quarter of 2026.
quotes: The impacts of these system disruptions included order processing, shipping, and invoicing delays, resulting in a negative impact on net sales and operating profit during the second quarter, particularly within the Consumer Products segment.
As a result, our products and entertainment offerings can have short consumer life cycles with no guarantee of success.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Items 1A and 7 and the third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q financial statements and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Cost of sales (1,296.2 (table in millions) in 2025 and 893.3 (table in millions) in the first nine months of 2026) and Selling, distribution and administration (1,173.9 (table in millions) in 2025 and 929.3 (table in millions) in the first nine months of 2026) are the largest ongoing operating costs, with Cost of sales exposed to third-party Far East manufacturing and tariffs ($44.9 million of tariff costs in 2025 versus $54.5 million of tariff recoveries in the third quarter of 2026).
quotes: Additionally, we utilize third-party manufacturers primarily located in the Far East, including China, Vietnam and India, to produce most of our products.
The Company recognized approximately $44.9 million of tariff costs within Cost of sales during 2025.

During the three and nine months ended September 27, 2026, Hasbro recorded a total of $54.5 million of tariff recoveries as a reduction to Cost of sales within the Consolidated Statements of Operations.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Items 1A and 7 and the third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q income statement.
business_model.claim: Royalties rose from $284.2 million (6.9% of net revenues) in 2024 to $368.9 million (7.8% of net revenues) in 2025, and reached 309.7 (table in millions) in the first nine months of 2026, driven by sales of products using third-party IP such as MAGIC: THE GATHERING Universes Beyond sets and minimum royalty guarantees.
quotes: The increase in Royalties in dollars and as a percent of net revenues during 2025 directly reflects the impact of increased sales relating to MAGIC: THE GATHERING Universes Beyond sets, such as Final Fantasy, Avatar: The Last Airbender and Marvel's Spider-Man, for which the Company is obligated to pay a royalty.

The license agreements we enter to obtain these rights usually require us to pay minimum royalty guarantees that may be substantial, and in some cases may be greater than what we are ultimately able to recoup from actual sales, which could result in write-offs and could harm our results of operations.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 7 MD&A and the third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q income statement and MD&A.
business_model.claim: Product development expense increased from $294.1 million in 2024 to $385.6 million in 2025 (and totaled 275.0 (table in millions) in the first nine months of 2026) due to internal digital game development, which also carries software write-off risk as seen in the $56.4 million non-cash impairment recorded in the second quarter of 2026.
quotes: The increase in Product development expense during 2025 was driven by incremental investments in the development of digital game titles that have not yet met technological feasibility.

The increase in Operating profit for the nine months ended September 27, 2026 was also impacted by a one-time $1,021.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment recorded in the Consumer Products segment in the second quarter of 2025 which did not recur in 2026, partially offset by a one-time $56.4 million non-cash impairment charge in the second quarter of 2026 related to the Company's decision to refocus the Digital Games portfolio.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 Business and the third quarter 2026 Form 10-Q MD&A.
business_model.claim: Hasbro offsets operating costs through its Operational Excellence program—which delivered almost $800 million of gross cost savings through 2025 toward a $1.0 billion commitment and cut content spend over 90% after divesting eOne Film and TV—while incurring $11.8 million in incremental expenses during the first nine months of 2026 to remediate the March 2026 network incident.
quotes: Through 2025, we have delivered almost $800 million of gross cost savings and are well on our path to our previous $1.0 billion commitment.

Divestiture of the non-core film and TV business of eOne (as defined below) which returned “play” to the center of our mission and investment priorities, ultimately reducing content spend by over 90%.

The Company incurred incremental expenses of approximately $1.0 million and $11.8 million, respectively, during the three and nine months ended September 27, 2026 as a result of the unauthorized access, including for third-party IT recovery and forensic experts, professional services and other costs incurred to investigate and remediate the attack.

competitive_position.claim: Hasbro states it possesses competitive advantages across its brand portfolio, licensing business, and games business, anchored by Magic: The Gathering, Dungeons & Dragons, Monopoly, and Hasbro gaming classics.
quotes: As a Company, we possess three competitive advantages: 1) a broad and deep brand portfolio rooted in play; 2) one of the biggest and most diverse licensing businesses in the world and 3) a profitable games business anchored by MAGIC: THE GATHERING, DUNGEONS & DRAGONS, MONOPOLY, and Hasbro gaming classics.
Our competitive advantages reinforce one another.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, P4, and P6
competitive_position.claim: Hasbro combines owned franchises such as Magic: The Gathering, Monopoly, Play-Doh, Transformers, Dungeons & Dragons, Nerf, and Peppa Pig with third-party licensed brands and reaches more than 1 billion fans annually.
quotes: Through our franchise-first approach, we unlock value from both new and legacy IP, including MAGIC: THE GATHERING, MONOPOLY, HASBRO GAMES, PLAY-DOH, TRANSFORMERS, DUNGEONS & DRAGONS, NERF, and PEPPA PIG, as well as premier partner brands.

With 165 years of expertise, Hasbro delivers groundbreaking play experiences and reaches more than 1 billion fans annually around the world, through physical and digital games, video games, toys, licensed consumer products, location-based entertainment, film, TV and more.

competitive_position.claim: In 2025, the Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment grew net revenues by 44.7% to $2,186.9 (table in millions) with a 46.0% operating margin, led by a $641.5 million net revenue increase in Magic: The Gathering.
quotes: Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment net revenues increased 44.7% in 2025 compared to 2024.
Segment operating profit margin increased to 46.0% in 2025 from 41.8% in 2024, primarily driven by increased net revenue and product mix in 2025 as compared to 2024.

competitive_position.claim: In third quarter 2026, Magic: The Gathering topped $600 million in quarterly revenue for the first time at $616.1 (table in millions), up 34%, while Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming achieved a 49.2% operating margin.
quotes: We delivered a fourth consecutive quarter of double-digit revenue growth, and Magic: The Gathering topped $600 million in quarterly revenue for the first time.

The net revenue increase primarily reflects higher net revenues from Magic: The Gathering, which grew by $156.7 million, or 34.1%, driven by strong performance of the Universes Beyond The Hobbit set released during the quarter, as well as Reality Fracture.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P6
competitive_position.claim: Hasbro extends its IP through an asset-light out-licensing model in consumer products, digital games, and location-based entertainment, including Monopoly Go!, which generated $168.0 million of revenue in 2025 and $127 million year-to-date in 2026.
quotes: Our asset-light licensing model lets great partners extend our brands while we focus on what we do best.

These experiences bring our brands to life and further immerse our consumers in our storytelling in a capital efficient manner as the third-parties operating these experiences are making the investment in these initiatives.
Year-to-date Monopoly Go! contributed $127 million of revenue.

competitive_position.claim: Hasbro operates direct-to-consumer platforms—Magic: The Gathering Arena, Secret Lair, D&D Beyond, and Hasbro PULSE—to build direct fan relationships and sell exclusive or digital offerings beyond traditional retail.
quotes: Connecting with fans directly makes our products more accessible in more markets and enables us to sell brands and showcase selected items, creating more brand awareness while gaining a deeper understanding of our fans and what they want and expect from Hasbro.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P1, P3, and P6
competitive_position.claim: Hasbro delivered almost $800 million of gross cost savings through 2025 toward its $1.0 billion commitment, helping lift Consumer Products operating margin from (38.7)% in 2025 to 21.0% in third quarter 2026 (including a $48 million tariff refund benefit).
quotes: Through 2025, we have delivered almost $800 million of gross cost savings and are well on our path to our previous $1.0 billion commitment.
Operating profit of $174 million and Adjusted operating profit of $178 million (+100% vs. LY) driven by productivity initiatives.
Operating profit and adjusted operating profit include a $48 million benefit from tariff refunds.

competitive_position.claim: Hasbro faces intense competition with low barriers to entry from large toy and digital gaming rivals, private-label retailers, influencers on platforms like TikTok, and competitors using AI to develop products more rapidly.
quotes: In addition to existing competitors, the barriers to entry for new participants in the play industry are low.

For example, with the use of influencers and media outlets such as Tik Tok, new participants with a popular product idea can gain access to consumers and become a significant source of competition for our products in a very short period of time.
We expect that as the use of artificial intelligence becomes more prevalent, we will continue to see increased competition from those using such technology to develop games, toys and content.

competitive_position.claim: Rapidly evolving consumer preferences, short product life cycles, and frequent cross-brand collaborations or expanded licensing risk causing franchise fatigue and oversaturation that erode brand value.
quotes: As a result, our products and entertainment offerings can have short consumer life cycles with no guarantee of success.

In addition, frequent product releases, cross-brand collaborations or expanded licensing initiatives may contribute to franchise fatigue or oversaturation, which could reduce long-term consumer engagement and diminish the value of our brands.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2 and P6, and observed in F2 and P6 revenue tables
competitive_position.claim: Hasbro's growth strategy concentrates sales and profits in key franchises such as Magic: The Gathering, which accounted for $1,630.9 (table in millions) of the $3,735.1 (table in millions) total net revenues in the first nine months of 2026.
quotes: Because our strategy emphasizes growing a focused set of franchises and expanding our higher-margin games and digital businesses, including MAGIC: THE GATHERING and DUNGEONS & DRAGONS, adverse trends affecting consumer demand for, or engagement with, any of these key brands could disproportionately impact our results of operations.

•our ability to continually introduce new and innovative products that are accepted by consumers, particularly for brands such as Magic: The Gathering in which we have seen an increasing concentration of our sales and profits;

competitive_position.claim: Developing digital games internally carries higher costs, longer timelines, and narrow launch windows, which led to a $56.4 million non-cash impairment charge in 2026 when Hasbro refocused its Digital Games portfolio.
quotes: As a result, we face the risk of significant write-offs in the event a digital game’s development is discontinued prior to commercialization or is not as commercially successful as we planned.

The increase in Operating profit for the nine months ended September 27, 2026 was also impacted by a one-time $1,021.9 million non-cash goodwill impairment recorded in the Consumer Products segment in the second quarter of 2025 which did not recur in 2026, partially offset by a one-time $56.4 million non-cash impairment charge in the second quarter of 2026 related to the Company's decision to refocus the Digital Games portfolio.

competitive_position.claim: Hasbro relies on a concentrated customer base with no binding long-term purchase commitments, with Amazon.com, Inc. and Wal-Mart, Inc. accounting for approximately 11% and 9% of consolidated net revenues in 2025, alongside dependence on specialty hobby stores for Wizards.
quotes: During 2025, Amazon.com, Inc. and Wal-Mart, Inc. accounted for approximately 11% and 9%, respectively, of our consolidated net revenues.
Similarly, sales of certain products of our Wizards business depend in part on the success of specialty hobby stores.
Our customers generally do not enter into binding long-term purchase commitments with us and make all purchases by delivering purchase orders.

competitive_position.claim: Competition for third-party IP licenses is intense and often requires substantial minimum guaranteed royalties that may not be recouped if licensed products underperform, while royalty expenses rose to $368.9 million in 2025 alongside Universes Beyond sets.
quotes: In addition, competition in our industry for access to premium brand properties is intense and can lessen our ability to secure, maintain, and renew popular licenses on beneficial terms.

The license agreements we enter to obtain these rights usually require us to pay minimum royalty guarantees that may be substantial, and in some cases may be greater than what we are ultimately able to recoup from actual sales, which could result in write-offs and could harm our results of operations.
Royalties totaled $368.9 million, or 7.8% of net revenues, in 2025 compared to $284.2 million, or 6.9% of net revenues, in 2024.

competitive_position.claim: Out-licensing brands to third parties reduces Hasbro's control over brand quality and representation and exposes it to partner non-payment, IP infringement, or reduced partner investment.
quotes: Under these and other partner arrangements, we lose some control over how the brand or intellectual property is used, potentially leading to misuse or misrepresentation.

As our strategy increasingly relies on third-party partners to invest in and scale experiences based on our intellectual property, reductions in partner investment, shifts in partner priorities or changes in economic conditions could limit the growth, reach or profitability of these initiatives.

competitive_position.claim: Hasbro relies on third-party manufacturers concentrated in China (along with Vietnam, India, and Japan) and increasing use of original design manufacturers, creating sourcing transition delays and reduced direct control over quality and design.
quotes: Most of our toy and game products are manufactured by third-party manufacturers, a substantial but decreasing number of which are in China, and a significant amount of our product sourcing also coming from manufacturers in the U.S., Vietnam, India and Japan.

In addition, our increased use of original design manufacturers ("ODMs") to support cost efficiency and speed to market may reduce our direct control over product design, quality, sourcing and manufacturing processes, and any failure by ODM partners to meet our design specifications, quality standards, delivery requirements or compliance obligations could adversely affect our products, brand reputation, margins and results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: stated in P2, P4, and P6

quotes: The use of artificial intelligence in product and game development may also raise intellectual property, data sourcing, ethical or regulatory issues, and disputes or restrictions in these areas could increase costs, delay development or limit the use of certain technologies.

risks relating to new and evolving laws and regulations governing artificial intelligence, children’s privacy and online safety, including state legislation specifically regulating artificial intelligence features in products marketed to or used by children, which may require pre-market assessments, restrict data collection or product functionality, impose civil penalties or product recalls, vary across jurisdictions, increase our compliance costs, delay or prevent product launches or limit the features we are able to offer;

competitive_position.claim: Simultaneously executing multiple strategic initiatives alongside recent workforce reductions and the planned relocation of Rhode Island operations to Boston, Massachusetts risks straining management capacity and losing key personnel and institutional skills.
quotes: In addition, the simultaneous pursuit of multiple strategic initiatives, including digital gaming development, licensing expansion, AI adoption, systems modernization and cost-saving initiatives, may strain management attention, organizational capacity and capital resources, and any failure to appropriately prioritize or allocate resources among these initiatives could adversely affect our business and result of operations.

our business could be adversely affected by challenges and disruptions arising from the loss of skills, knowledge or expertise, and from uncertainty regarding the continued employment of key personnel, particularly as a result of recent workforce reductions and the planned relocation of our Rhode Island operations to Boston, Massachusetts;
